scope: Windows resource probe timeout process cleanup; real test-created processes only; no production process action

diagnostic_observations_before_change.method: Ten real venv Python launches observed with a native interpreter process handle opened while that interpreter was alive. Timeout OSError objects and real Popen objects were retained. Each interpreter handle was closed after exit. Tool-output observations summarized here; this is not an additional pytest run.
diagnostic_observations_before_change.interpretation: PID enumeration alone does not establish a live process. The venv launcher and interpreter are distinct, and launcher job termination completes asynchronously. Popen keeps the launcher process handle open until finalization even after confirmed exit; holding error tracebacks prolongs this retention.

repair.runtime: After bounded pipe-reader joins, close the Popen-owned Windows process handle only when returncode confirms process termination and every reader has exited. A still-running reader can be inside process.kill, so it retains normal Popen handle ownership instead. Use Handle.Close so finalization remains idempotent; do not close raw handles behind Popen.
repair.test_oracle: Capture the actual Windows interpreter handle while live, verify it signals within a bounded one-second wait, verify exited status, and retain the existing three-second total test deadline. Preserve the venv launcher topology. Cleanup can terminate only the same captured test-process handle if the assertion fails.
repair.lifecycle_regressions: Real success, nonzero exit, output-limit, and timeout cases retain Popen references and failure tracebacks while verifying that handles and pipes were explicitly closed.

limitations: No privileged acceptance or hardware-driver/sensor access was performed.
This does not establish a generic descendant-process termination contract. Production helper commands remain controlled direct native executables.
The prior failing consolidated result remains preserved; a fresh consolidated run is required for the changed source.

primary_sources.supports: Windows venv launcher starts the interpreter in a kill-on-close job.
Popen stores a Windows Handle object; Handle.Close is idempotent; wait records returncode while handle lifetime normally follows object lifetime.
Termination closes handles owned by the process; a process object remains until its open handles close.
A process handle becomes signaled when the process terminates; bounded native handle waiting avoids PID reuse ambiguity.
Windows PID existence can fall back to enumeration even when a process exit code is no longer STILL_ACTIVE.

independent_review.result: Native interpreter handle and retained traceback proofs accepted. One potential close-while-reader-kill race identified and repaired before final validation by requiring every reader exited. No other defect found.
